react_result.final_narrative_text: Four independent pathway-enrichment tools converge on arachidonic acid metabolism as the dominant biological signal in this differential-metabolomics dataset. RaMP multi-database ORA reports Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) as the top hit with an FDR of 2.12×10⁻¹³ and a fold-enrichment of 1251, driven by five input metabolites (arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-PGJ2, 5-HETE, 15-HETE). The same five metabolites reproduce across SMPDB drug-action pathway clusters (rofecoxib, acetylsalicylic acid, acetaminophen, etc.) — these are not independent findings but variant labels on the identical hit set, all sharing the same five eicosanoids. Mummichog, using m/z-direct activity scoring on the human_mfn empirical network, independently ranks "Arachidonic acid metabolism" first (p=0.0065, 11 matched nodes) and additionally flags "Prostaglandin formation from arachidonate" (p=0.040) and "Leukotriene metabolism" (p=0.040). MetaboAnalystR PSEA confirms KEGG:hsa00590 "Arachidonic acid metabolism" as the top KEGG-classified pathway (p=0.0396, 4 metabolites: arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 15-HETE, 5-HETE). Xanthine and thiosulfate appear as secondary signals restricted to single-tool hits (sulfur metabolism, purine metabolism, respectively) and do not replicate across paradigms. The androgen 5-androstenediol and the organic acid methylmalonic acid do not reach significance in any tool. The three-tools consensus is therefore a single, robust biological story: arachidonic acid is released and shunted into the cyclooxygenase and lipoxygenase branches, producing elevated leukotriene A4, 5-HETE, 15-HETE, and 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-PGJ2 — consistent with a pro-inflammatory or COX/LOX-inhibited state. InChIKey reconciliation confirmed all five driver metabolites are structurally distinct (zero conflicts), ruling out namespace artefacts.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent pathway-analysis tools (RaMP multi-DB ORA, Mummichog m/z-based network activity, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA) converge on arachidonic acid as the dominant signal. RaMP reports WP:WP167 Eicosanoid synthesis as the top hit (FDR=2.12×10⁻¹³, fold-enrichment=1250.95) driven by five input metabolites: arachidonic acid (KEGG:C00219), leukotriene A4 (KEGG:C00909), 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-PGJ2 (KEGG:C14717), 5-HETE (KEGG:C04805), and 15-HETE (KEGG:C04742). Mummichog independently returns MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism with p=5.04×10⁻⁴ and 11 matched nodes, fully overlapping the input set. MetaboAnalystR PSEA confirms KEGG:hsa00590 with p=2.49×10⁻⁶ and four metabolites, consistent with the same metabolic branch. Secondary Mummichog hits include Leukotriene metabolism (p=0.019) and Prostaglandin formation from arachidonate (p=0.025). The SMPDB Rofecoxib Action Pathway (rank 2) and Leukotriene C4 Synthesis Deficiency (rank 1) both share the identical five-driver metabolite set, indicating convergence across drug-action and metabolic-dysfunction annotations. Thiosulfate, methylmalonic acid, 5-androstenediol, and xanthine did not reach significance in any tool.

payload_summary.fallback_suggested: FELLA R subprocess errored at runtime (currently 'argument is of length zero' on every sub6b-v3 task — W9 D4 stretch target); skip the network/diffusion paradigm and rely on ORA + mummichog

pathway_members.sqlite only indexes HUMAN1 + RECON2; for namespace 'WP', inspect the `metabolites_hit` list inside an EnrichmentResult (e.g. from run_ramp_enrichment) — it carries the method-specific compound roster
use run_ramp_enrichment (multi-DB ORA, broader namespace coverage) or run_metaboanalystr_psea (KEGG-specific ORA) instead
